newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Regional security concerns hit Kuwait share index.
newsitem.headline: Regional security concerns hit Kuwait share index.

text.p: Kuwait's share index fell 4.5 percent in the week ending on Wednesday as Gulf Arab politicians expressed concern over regional stability, figures released by the stock exchange on Thursday showed.
The index fell 83.2 points to 1,830 points. Decliners outpaced gainers 45-2, while four stocks were unchanged.
"Warnings by politicians are not helping," one dealer said.
A Gulf official said on Sunday Iran's moves to bolster its "occupation" of Gulf islands claimed by the United Arab Emirates could threaten regional security.
Kuwaiti officials also reiterated their concern over the intentions of Iraq, the tiny state's neighbour and former occupier.
"If you look at economic indicators they are generally good," said one portfolio manager. "The economy is OK."

The Kuwait Investment Authority said on Tuesday Kuwait would finish repaying a $5.5 billion sovereign loan on time this month without having to sell assets or seek further loans, saying the economy had recovered from Iraq's 1990-91 occupation.
Economists have been expecting a correction on the stock market after an upward trend that prevailed for several weeks in October and November.
The total value of traded shares eased to 108.8 million dinars ($363.8 million) from 136.7 million in the previous week. Volume fell to 377.4 million shares from 497.6 million.
By sector, banks led trading by value, with 42.1 million dinars, followed by service sector firms with 20.1 million and investment companies with 19.8 million.
The Commercial Bank, Gulf Bank, Investment Projects, The International Investor and United Realty were among the most actively traded shares.
Only nationals of Gulf Arab states -- Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Oman and Kuwait -- can trade on the exchange. Foreign residents can invest through mutual funds.
Kuwait is considering opening trade to foreign investors. ($1 = 0.299 dinar)
